record.summary: Bill passed by the Legislature in August 2024 that would have required developers of the most advanced AI models, those costing over $100 million to train, to guard against critical harms: before training, protect models against unauthorised access and misuse, build in the capability for a full shutdown and adopt a written safety and security protocol, with third-party audits and AI safety incidents reported within 72 hours. It would also have created the Board of Frontier Models, whistleblower protections for employees of frontier AI laboratories and the CalCompute public computing cluster. The Governor vetoed it.
record.notes: Sent to the Governor after the Senate's 29-9 vote announced on 29 Aug 2024, and vetoed on 29 Sep 2024 (date_published is the veto date). The veto message objects that the bill covered only the most expensive and large-scale models, whether or not a system is deployed in high-risk environments, involves critical decision-making or uses sensitive data, warns that smaller, specialised models may prove as dangerous, and asks for an approach informed by an empirical trajectory analysis of AI systems and capabilities. The same day the Governor announced that Fei-Fei Li, Mariano-Florentino Cuéllar and Jennifer Tour Chayes would help lead California's effort to develop guardrails for generative AI; their report followed in June 2025 (US-CA-04). Included for historical context.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored and read: the Governor's veto message (gov.ca.gov PDF, stamped 29 Sep 2024), which gives the bill number, the veto, the Board of Frontier Models and the reasons; the Governor's release of 29 Sep 2024 (gov.ca.gov), which announces the veto and the experts; Senator Wiener's release of 29 Aug 2024 (sd11.senate.ca.gov), which gives the final Senate vote, the $100 million threshold, CalCompute and the whistleblower protections; and the Assembly Privacy and Consumer Protection Committee's analysis (hearing of 18 Jun 2024, apcp.assembly.ca.gov), which gives the title as its subject and describes the full-shutdown, safety and security protocol, third-party audit, 72-hour incident-reporting and Board duties. That analysis describes the bill as amended on 5 Jun 2024 and proposed to be amended, not the enrolled bill the Governor vetoed, so the summary's specific duties rest on an earlier version (see open questions). The enrolled text on leginfo.legislature.ca.gov refused automated downloads (HTTP 403).

summary.quote: SACRAMENTO – In a bipartisan vote, the landmark California AI safety bill, SB 1047 by Senator Scott Wiener (D-San Francisco), passed the Senate 29-9.
The bill heads next to the Governor.
The legislation would cover only the most powerful AI systems, costing over $100 million to train.
SB 1047 would require developers of the most advanced AI systems to test their models for the ability to cause critical harm.

Requires that before a developer initially trains a covered model, they do all of the following: a) Implement protections to prevent unauthorized access, misuse, or unsafe post-training modification of the covered model
b) Implement the capability to enact a full shutdown. c) Implement a written safety and security protocol
responsible for ensuring compliance, including by conducting third party audits.
Requires a developer of a covered model to report each artificial intelligence safety incident to the Frontier Model Division within 72 hours of the developer learning of the safety incident.

This bill would require developers of large artificial intelligence (Al) models, and those providing the computing power to train such models, to put certain safeguards and policies in place to prevent catastrophic harm . The bill would also establish the Board of Frontier Models
Establishes the Board of Frontier Models in the Government Operations Agency.
it would also create whistleblower protections for employees of frontier AI laboratories.
The bill would also establish a new public cloud computing cluster, CalCompute
I am returning Senate Bill 1047 without my signature.

notes.quote: SACRAMENTO – In a bipartisan vote, the landmark California AI safety bill, SB 1047 by Senator Scott Wiener (D-San Francisco), passed the Senate 29-9.
SEP 2 9 2024 To the Members of the California State Senate: I am returning Senate Bill 1047 without my signature.

By focusing only on the most expensive and large-scale models, SB 1047 establishes a regulatory framework that could give the public a false sense of security about controlling this fast-moving technology.
Smaller, specialized models may emerge as equally or even more dangerous than the models targeted by SB 1047
While well-intentioned, SB 1047 does not take into account whether an Al system is deployed in high-risk environments, involves critical decision-making or the use of sensitive data.
I do not agree, however, that to keep the public safe, we must settle for a solution that is not informed by an empirical trajectory analysis of Al systems and capabilities.
